s1.syndrome_frame: Systemic infection with multi-organ involvement and sepsis in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: Acute hypoxic respiratory failure and septic shock
key_facts: Patient has HIV/AIDS with CD4 count <20 cells/µL
Patient has a history of intravenous drug use
Patient has active tobacco dependence
Patient reported one month of poor appetite and weight loss
Patient reported subjective fevers
Patient had diarrhea without abdominal pain, vomiting, cough, or dyspnea
Patient was febrile (39.4 °C) and hypotensive (91/60 mmHg)
Patient had leukocytosis (31 151/µL) and hyponatremia (Na 121 mEq/L)
Chest radiograph was clear initially
Abdominal ultrasound showed hepatosplenomegaly, ascites, and enlarged peripancreatic lymph nodes
Patient developed acute hypoxic respiratory failure and septic shock
Blood cultures remained negative
Lumbar puncture showed elevated opening pressure and RBCs

shortlist.label: Disseminated tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has HIV/AIDS with low CD4 count and symptoms consistent with disseminated TB

shortlist.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has HIV/AIDS with low CD4 count and respiratory symptoms, although BAL was negative

shortlist.label: Mycobacterium avium complex infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has HIV/AIDS with low CD4 count and systemic infection symptoms

shortlist.label: Cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has HIV/AIDS with low CD4 count and symptoms consistent with cryptococcal infection, including elevated intracranial pressure

shortlist.label: Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has HIV/AIDS with low CD4 count and symptoms consistent with toxoplasmosis, including fever and neurological symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of fever, weight loss, and poor appetite, combined with the findings of hepatosplenomegaly and ascites on abdominal ultrasound, are consistent with disseminated tuberculosis, particularly in the context of a severely immunocompromised patient with HIV/AIDS and a history of intravenous drug use.

rejected.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
rejected.why: Bronchoalveolar lavage was negative for Pneumocystis jirovecii cultures

rejected.label: Mycobacterium avium complex infection
rejected.why: While possible in an immunocompromised patient, the clinical presentation and laboratory findings do not specifically point to this diagnosis

rejected.label: Cryptococcosis
rejected.why: The lumbar puncture findings could suggest cryptococcal meningitis, but the absence of specific evidence such as positive cryptococcal antigen or culture makes this less likely

rejected.label: Toxoplasmosis
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence provided that would strongly support toxoplasmosis, such as characteristic lesions on imaging or positive serology
